findings.description: The instance user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext values. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (including via SSRF), and the secrets are also stored in Terraform state and the EC2 API.

No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is configured and no IMDSv2 enforcement (metadata_options http_tokens = required) is set, leaving the root volume data unencrypted at rest and the instance metadata (including the hard-coded credentials) reachable via IMDSv1 SSRF.

The instance is launched into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH, so it receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet.
Ingress rule allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploit attempts against the host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no TLS listener configured, so web traffic to the host is transmitted in cleartext.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted outbound connections that facilitate data exfiltration and command-and-control from a compromised host.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data attached to the web host is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is configured, so a copy of the volume data is persisted unencrypted and could be shared or restored by anyone with snapshot access.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and access controls
findings.description: The VPC flow-log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, no versioning and no enforced TLS-only bucket policy, leaving network telemetry unprotected at rest and vulnerable to accidental public exposure or deletion (force_destroy = true).
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the network boundary for workloads that do not need internet exposure.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, exposing workloads directly to the internet by default.
